title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: When a Telex Release Has Taken Effect
content:
The telex release fee on a `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` record is owed only for a release that has taken effect. This page defines the state of the record in which a telex release has taken effect.

## Definition

A telex release has taken effect when all of the following are true on the line's records at the time of charging:

1. the document stands in the status surrendered;
2. the document shows that none of its originals is left in circulation;
3. the document's type offers the telex release;
4. the booking behind the document stands far enough along for the telex release charge.

## Consequence for the fee

As long as a telex release has not taken effect, the fee amount is zero and no fee entry is booked. The fee attaches only to a record in the state described above.

## Condition table (hypothetical records)

| Document status | Originals left in circulation | Type offers telex release | Booking far enough along | Taken effect? | Fee entry |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Surrendered | 0 | Yes | Yes | Yes | May be booked |
| Issued | 3 | Yes | Yes | No | None |
| Issued | 0 | Yes | Yes | No | None |
| Surrendered | 0 | No | Yes | No | None |
| Surrendered | 0 | Yes | No | No | None |

## Points of judgement

**The request was registered days ago and the shipper promised to bring the originals. Has the release taken effect?** No. A registered request alone changes nothing; the record must show the document surrendered with no original left in circulation.

**The document is issued and shows no originals left in circulation. Is that enough?** No. The status must be surrendered as well.
